headline: Bias, prejudice, discrimination · 02:51

items.title: 02:51 · The American Psychological Association Dictionary defines ingroup
items.detail: The American Psychological Association Dictionary defines ingroup bias as the tendency to favor one's own group and its members in resource allocation, evaluation, and attribution.

items.title: 03:01 · Henri Tajfel and John Turner formalized this
items.detail: Henri Tajfel and John Turner formalized this dynamic in their 1979 formulation of Social Identity Theory within the psychology of intergroup relations.

items.title: 03:10 · Social Identity Theory demonstrates that human beings
items.detail: Social Identity Theory demonstrates that human beings sort their social environment into us and them with remarkable speed and minimal situational prompting.

items.title: 03:18 · That sorting mechanism evolved in small-scale coalitional
items.detail: That sorting mechanism evolved in small-scale coalitional environments to manage trust, threat detection, reciprocity, belonging, and individual self-concept inside bounded groups.

items.title: 03:27 · In the terminology of the book s
items.detail: In the terminology of the book's Preface, the human brain operates as biological host wetware: a predictive, pattern-compressing neural network tuned for fast categorization.
